newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cotton planting progresses steadily in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cotton planting progresses steadily in week.

text.p: Cotton planting progressed steadily in most U.S. producer states in the week ended May 25 with rainfall in some states a welcome relief, according to weekly crop reports from state agricultural statistics services.

MISSISSIPPI - Cotton was 99 percent planted versus 89 a week ago, 99 a year ago and 93 on a 5-year average. Cotton was 82 percent emerged vs 46 last week, 96 last year and 83 average. Crop conditions were rated 13 percent excellent, 71 good, 15 fair and one poor. Rain during the past week was a welcome relief to most farmers across the state. Soil moisture conditions were rated 7 percent short, 64 percent adequate, and 29 percent surplus.

LOUISIANA - Heavy rains across the state allowed fieldwork to proceed for only four days last week. Cotton was rated 4 percent excellent, 74 good, 21 fair and 1 poor. Soil moisture was 6 percent short, 63 adequate and 31 surplus. Cotton planting was hindered by the rains. Crops were 98 percent planted versus 90 last week, 99 last year and a five year average of 97. Cotton was 83 percent emerged versus 96 last year and an average of 92.

TEXAS - 54 percent of the cotton crop was planted for 1997, compared with 48 last year and a five year average of 55. Statewide cotton conditions were rated at 14 percent excellent, 52 good, 28 fair and 6 poor. There were no crop conditions rated very poor for cotton. Planting was active in the Plains as conditions improved by late week. Warm temperatures in Central areas benefitted the crop.

CALIFORNIA - Sunny skies and slightly cooler temperatures were perfect for field crop activities. The warm weather encouraged rapid growth in cotton, and growers continued cultivating, irrigating, weeding and treating emerged fields for aphids and mites.

ARIZONA - Cotton development progress advanced to 32 percent squaring compared to 30 percent last year and 17 average. Some fields in the west and central areas were beginning to set bolls. Crop condition rated 1 percent very poor, 1 poor, 18 fair, 54 good and 26 excellent. Temperatures were more mild this week with some areas receiving rainfall.
Average temperatures were 1 degree below normal to 6 degrees above normal statewide compared to 5 to 13 degrees above normal the previous week.
